"Techno" is not one sound. Cities, clubs, machines and people each pulled it a different way, and DJs and fans named the results.
This lesson is an **investigation**: for each subgenre you get a question, a few traits to listen for, names to look up, and one
change to make to the techno beat below. **Write your prediction first**, then make the change and listen.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Facts on this page are unverified
This page was written without being able to check its sources. Every date, name, place and tempo marked *(unverified)* is
the usual story as commonly told, not yet checked against the sources listed under Works Cited. Treat them as leads to research,
and checking them is part of the inquiry.
:::

## The beat you will change

The DAW holds an eight-bar techno loop at 130 bpm: kick on every beat, open hat on the off-beats, shaker, ride, a rolling bass,
a rim shot and a cowbell. Each sound is its own track, so you can mute, change notes and velocities, or change the tempo.
Reset (in the DAW) brings it back between experiments.

<div class="mdaw" data-id="daw-remix-subgenres" data-preset="techno" data-show="transport tracks editor mixer"></div>

**Prediction log.** For each experiment write three lines: *I will change…*, *I predict it will sound…*, *It actually sounded…*.

## Detroit techno

**Guiding question:** what makes machine music sound *hopeful* or *futuristic* instead of cold?

- **Where and when:** Detroit, mid-1980s *(unverified)*. Usually credited to three friends from Belleville, Michigan,
  Juan Atkins, Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson *(unverified)*.
- **Tempo:** roughly 120-135 bpm *(unverified)*.
- **Listen for:** drum machines (often named: Roland TR-808 and TR-909, *unverified*), string-like synth chords, a melody over a
  steady machine beat; a sense of space and future.
- **Names to look up:** Juan Atkins / Model 500; Derrick May / Rhythim Is Rhythim; Kevin Saunderson / Inner City; Underground Resistance.

**Try it in the DAW.** Add a new track on the Electric piano or Organ and write one long chord per two bars (for example A minor, then
F major). *Predict:* does the beat feel more like a song, or less like techno? Then lower the tempo to 125.

## Acid techno and acid house

**Guiding question:** how can one bass line be the whole piece?

- **Where and when:** acid house began in Chicago in the mid-1980s *(unverified)*; acid techno is a harder, faster cousin from the
  1990s *(unverified)*.
- **The machine:** the Roland TB-303 bass synth, its filter turned up so the line "squelches" *(unverified)*.
- **Tempo:** acid house about 120-128, acid techno 130-150 *(unverified)*.
- **Names to look up:** Phuture, "Acid Tracks"; Hardfloor; Josh Wink.

**Try it in the DAW.** This DAW has no filter knob, so build the squelch out of notes: open the Rolling bass clip and make every
sixteenth a note, jump some up an octave, and give them very different **velocities** (some loud accents, many quiet).
Make a few notes overlap the next one (that is how a 303 "slides"). *Predict:* will it sound more like a melody or more like a rhythm?

## Minimal techno

**Guiding question:** how little can you keep and still make people dance?

- **Where and when:** early-to-mid 1990s, linked to Detroit (Robert Hood) and to Richie Hawtin and Daniel Bell *(unverified)*;
  later big in Berlin and Cologne *(unverified)*.
- **Tempo:** about 120-130 bpm *(unverified)*.
- **Listen for:** very few sounds, small changes over a long time, clicks and short percussion, lots of silence between hits.
- **Names to look up:** Robert Hood, *Minimal Nation*; Plastikman; Ricardo Villalobos.

**Try it in the DAW.** **Mute** the shaker, ride and cowbell. Delete half the bass notes. Then every 4 bars bring *one* thing back
(unmute a track or add one rim hit). *Predict:* will it feel boring or hypnotic? How long before you notice a change?

## Dub techno

**Guiding question:** what does an echo add that another instrument cannot?

- **Where and when:** Berlin, early 1990s, Basic Channel (Moritz von Oswald and Mark Ernestus) *(unverified)*, borrowing from
  Jamaican dub's echo and reverb.
- **Tempo:** about 115-125 bpm *(unverified)*.
- **Listen for:** one short chord that repeats and fades into echoes, soft hiss, deep bass, a slow, foggy feel.
- **Names to look up:** Basic Channel; Rhythm & Sound; Deepchord; Monolake.

**Try it in the DAW.** There is no delay effect here, so **write the echo**: add a chord track, put one short chord on the *&* of
beat 1, then copy it 3/16 later at half the velocity, and again at a quarter. Lower the tempo to 120 and mute the ride.
*Predict:* does writing echoes by hand sound like a real delay? What gives it away?

## Hard and industrial techno

**Guiding question:** where is the line between loud and harsh, and why would a crowd want harsh?

- **Where and when:** industrial techno is often traced to Birmingham, England, in the 1990s (Regis, Surgeon) *(unverified)*;
  "hard techno" covers faster, heavier styles in many countries *(unverified)*.
- **Tempo:** 135-150 bpm or faster *(unverified)*.
- **Listen for:** distorted kicks, metallic noise, few or no chords, relentless energy.
- **Names to look up:** Surgeon; Regis; Ancient Methods; Perc.

**Try it in the DAW.** Raise the tempo to 145. Push the Kick track's fader up and make every kick full velocity; switch the bass track
to **Electric guitar (distorted)**. Put the rim on every off-beat. *Predict:* which change makes it sound "industrial", the tempo or the sound?

## Berlin / warehouse techno

**Guiding question:** how can a *place* become part of a genre?

- **Where and when:** after the Berlin Wall fell (1989), parties in empty buildings in the old East; clubs such as Tresor (1991)
  and later Berghain (2004) *(all unverified)*.
- **Tempo:** about 128-140 bpm *(unverified)*.
- **Listen for:** long DJ sets, rolling bass, dark and steady grooves made for a big concrete room.
- **Names to look up:** Ben Klock; Marcel Dettmann; Ellen Allien; the Tresor label.

**Try it in the DAW.** Keep the beat at 132 and make it **longer**: duplicate clips to 32 bars and change only one thing every 8 bars.
*Predict:* would this work in a three-minute song? Why does it work in a long night?

## Contrast: deep house and tech house

**Guiding question:** what has to change before techno turns into house?

- **Deep house:** Chicago and New York, mid-1980s; Larry Heard (Mr. Fingers) usually named *(unverified)*. Slower (about 115-125, *unverified*),
  warm jazz and soul chords, often vocals.
  Look up: Mr. Fingers, "Can You Feel It"; Kerri Chandler.
- **Tech house:** 1990s, mixing techno's machine sounds with house's swing and groove *(unverified)*; about 120-128 bpm *(unverified)*.
  Look up: Terry Francis; Fisher; Green Velvet.

**Try it in the DAW.** Lower the tempo to 122, add a clap on beats 2 and 4, and add a seventh chord (A C E G) on an Electric piano.
For tech house instead, keep the drums but shift every other closed-hat hit a little later (swing). *Predict:* at which change did you
start to hear house?

## Sort the sounds

Your teacher (or a partner) plays short clips, or you play each of your saved experiments. For each, decide which subgenre it is
closest to and give **two pieces of evidence** (tempo, a sound, how busy it is).

| Clue | Detroit | Acid | Minimal | Dub | Hard / industrial | Berlin | Deep house | Tech house |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tempo band | | | | | | | | |
| Main sound | | | | | | | | |
| How busy | | | | | | | | |
| One name | | | | | | | | |

Then line the subgenres up from **slowest to fastest** and from **fewest sounds to most**. Which two are closest? Which pair are opposites?

## Reflect

1. Which prediction was most wrong? What did you learn from it?
2. Is a subgenre defined more by tempo, by sounds, by place, or by the people? Use one example.
3. Pick one *(unverified)* fact on this page and check it: what did you find, and where?
4. Write three moves that would turn your techno beat into a subgenre of your own. Give it a name.

## In other DAWs

<div class="daw-map">

| | This DAW | BandLab | Ableton Live | Logic Pro |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 303-style squelch | Notes, octave jumps and velocities | A synth with filter resonance and envelope | A synth's filter resonance + envelope; slides with overlapping notes | Retro Synth or ES2: filter resonance + envelope; glide |
| Echo (dub) | Copy notes later and quieter | Delay effect | Delay / Echo effect | Tape Delay / Stereo Delay |
| Distortion (industrial) | Distorted-guitar sound, louder kick | Distortion effect | Saturator / Roar | Distortion / ChromaVerb plug-ins |
| Thinning out (minimal) | Mute, delete notes | Mute, delete | Mute, deactivate clips | Mute regions |

</div>
